headline: High-risk code-execution pair: AutoGen can write and egress by default, while awesome-selfhosted is an unverified knowledge source with no isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, so if it ingests content from awesome-selfhosted via copied files or shared workspace, attacker-controlled text could steer tool use. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source with no isolation metadata, so the bridge is plausible but not proven. This is weaker than high because no shared MCP or direct parser is documented.
conditions: IF AutoGen is configured to read content from a shared workspace populated by awesome-selfhosted entries
IF operator copies awesome-selfhosted text into AutoGen prompts or files without sanitization
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Strip instructions from imported knowledge entries
Require human review before AutoGen executes tool calls
Disable file-based ingestion for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and can write files with broad network egress, while awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source with no declared data handling controls. If AutoGen stores sensitive application data in a shared workspace that awesome-selfhosted indexes or exposes, leakage is plausible. The evidence is insufficient for high because awesome-selfhosted has no network egress and no sensitive-data handling is documented.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is placed in a workspace readable by both agents
IF AutoGen forwards file contents to external model providers while the same data is present in shared files
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories
Restrict AutoGen to a dedicated scratch directory
Turn off external model calls for sensitive runs
Review logs for accidental data capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is absent. However, if the pair is orchestrated around a shared mutable workspace, AutoGen can overwrite artifacts that awesome-selfhosted depends on for curation or indexing. Uncertainty about shared-state handling pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF awesome-selfhosted is used as a mutable index or generated artifact rather than a static list
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Make the knowledge source read-only
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Snapshot shared artifacts before AutoGen runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code and act through tools, and awesome-selfhosted can serve as an upstream knowledge source. If AutoGen's output is treated as authoritative by downstream curation or automation, errors can cascade into incorrect recommendations or actions. This is not high because awesome-selfhosted itself is not an action-taking agent, but the pair still creates an unverified-to-authoritative pipeline.
conditions: IF outputs from AutoGen are copied into awesome-selfhosted-derived curation without verification
IF downstream automation consumes AutoGen-generated recommendations as facts
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse
Add a human verification step
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted drafts
Compare against independent references
requires-engineering: add validation gates before publication

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and can send data to configured model providers, while awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge list with no residency or retention controls documented. The pair does not show a specific residency mismatch, but compliance gaps are possible if sensitive application data is routed through AutoGen and then reflected into the knowledge source. Only AutoGen is cited because the compliance risk is driven by its outbound handling; awesome-selfhosted lacks relevant controls to cite.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into AutoGen and then stored or published via the knowledge-management workflow
IF the configured model provider retains prompts beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts
Use a provider with a suitable DPA
Review retention settings before runs
Keep the knowledge list free of sensitive entries
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
